funFacts: Singapore Grand Prix is the original Formula 1 night race, running under 1,600 floodlights.
Marina Bay has featured at least one safety car in every single edition since its 2008 debut.
Drivers can lose up to three kilograms of body weight during the grueling two-hour race.

headline: Singapore GP Preview: Antonelli takes 88-point lead to Marina Bay night race
whyCareReason: Kimi Antonelli leads the Formula 1 World Championship into the grueling heat of Marina Bay as the Singapore Grand Prix night race looms.
teaser: Marina Bay Street Circuit, 2-4 October 2026. 62 laps under the lights with high humidity, safety cars, and an 88-point championship fight.
story:
Why this one matters: Formula 1 transitions from the high speeds of Baku directly into the grueling physical furnace of the Marina Bay Street Circuit for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix.

Fresh off his sensational victory in Azerbaijan, rookie phenom Kimi Antonelli arrives in Singapore commanding the World Championship with 317 points. Mercedes teammate George Russell trails at 229 points, with Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris fighting to stay within striking distance.

Marina Bay is historically one of the calendar's most unforgiving tests. Over 62 laps under blazing floodlights in 85% humidity, drivers face 19 corners with zero margin for error and a 100% historical safety car record. For Antonelli, managing tire degradation and street circuit walls will determine if his march toward the 2026 title continues unabated.
stakes: Antonelli seeks to extend his 88-point championship advantage while Ferrari and McLaren bring downforce upgrades to challenge Mercedes.
rivalryAngle: High-downforce street battle tests Mercedes straight-line superiority against McLaren and Ferrari agility.
